LinkedIn recruiting and candidate sourcing

Agree the role, approved sourcing tools and who can contact candidates before using LinkedIn in your recruitment workflow. For company posts, see LinkedIn publishing and engagement. For leads, see LinkedIn prospecting and sales support.

Build a relevant shortlist

Research profiles against the recruiter’s role criteria, document relevant experience and record the source in the applicant tracker.

Prepare outreach and keep the tracker current

Draft tailored messages for review, record approved outreach and responses and update interview status in the authorised system.

Hand candidates over to the hiring team

Send the shortlist, replies, outstanding questions and interview availability to the recruiter. The hiring team decides next steps.

When this support helps

Keep interviews on track

Confirm a slot with both sides, send the approved agenda and attach the right candidate material to the recruiter’s workspace.

Give a staffing team one view of open roles

Link job orders, approved postings, scheduled interviews and next steps so each hiring lead sees what needs attention.

Prepare a new hire’s first week

Track paperwork, training, equipment and access requests and send exceptions to the accountable team.

Planning your support

Open the topics that matter to your team. These details explain how to prepare the work, review results and handle changes.

Follow one vacancy from LinkedIn candidate sourcing to interview

In this fictional example, an operations role has been posted and the recruiter has an approved shortlist brief.

An applicant also appears in the LinkedIn candidate sourcing queue, one interviewer works in another time zone, and a reference is still outstanding. The shared hiring tracker keeps those details in one current record so the hiring lead can make the decisions.

  1. 01

    Open the role and connect the records

    A recruitment virtual assistant can confirm which brief is current, review the approved role fields and link the job posting to the applicant tracker. If someone applied directly and was also sourced, mark the possible duplicate and preserve their submission and contact history for the recruiter to review.

  2. 02

    Coordinate approved outreach and interviews

    Use LinkedIn candidate sourcing only through the agreed tools and access. Draft a role-specific introduction for review, then log any approved contact and reply. For interviews, confirm interviewer availability, the candidate’s time zone, format and meeting link. Put the current role brief and interview materials in the authorised workspace.

  3. 03

    Hand over what the recruiter needs next

    Bring the interview status, responses, reference requests and pending decisions together. Recruiting and people operations support can also prepare the onboarding checklist after the hiring lead confirms the selection. Keep the offer, employment terms and candidate evaluation with the authorised team.

Handle exceptions in LinkedIn candidate sourcing

Record the source, what you checked and who can decide. Keep blocked work visible until the next action changes.

The same candidate is in two queues

A recruitment virtual assistant can flag a match and link the relevant records without merging them or losing the applicant’s original messages. Show the last approved contact and next action. The recruiter decides how to combine the records and whether to continue outreach.

The role or timing changes mid-search

Update the LinkedIn candidate sourcing queue with the new brief and ask the recruiter to confirm what is on hold. Identify candidates with scheduled conversations or outstanding replies. Prepare an approved update for affected people and keep the old instructions with the record for reference.

A reference or document is sensitive

Use the approved channel and record the minimum status needed in the general tracker. A recruitment virtual assistant can follow up on authorised requests and show what is outstanding. The recruiter or HR owner decides what the material means and how it affects the process.

Set the scope for a recruitment virtual assistant

Role brief and communication rules

Give the recruitment virtual assistant the approved job description, required records, interview process and sender authority. Record which stage changes are routine administration and which need a recruiter’s decision. Share an approved invitation, reschedule notice and closure message so wording stays consistent.

Sourcing channels and applicant tracker

Agree the permitted LinkedIn candidate sourcing tools and how to record source, application date and contact history. Confirm who can access candidate records and how long the organisation keeps them. Use a test record to check which fields the assistant can edit or share.

Panel calendar and onboarding owners

Agree who can approve times, how to route last-minute changes and who owns follow-up when the recruiter is away. Recruiting and people operations support should also have an owner for each onboarding item, such as paperwork, training, equipment and access requests.

Review recruiting and people operations support

Check applicant records against the source

Sample a direct applicant, a sourced contact and an open exception. Verify source and last contact, role, stage and next action. Ask the recruitment virtual assistant to flag any fields that repeatedly go missing or have ambiguous definitions.

Check the interview handoff

Match the confirmed time, location or link and invitees to the appointment record. Recruiting and people operations support can gather feedback forms and flag missing responses. Confirm the next owner can access the material without circulating it more broadly.

Check sourcing and follow-up status

Review LinkedIn candidate sourcing with the recruiter. Separate records awaiting approved contact from records awaiting a reply or decision. Give each blocked item a due date and owner so a pending decision does not trigger a duplicate message.

Make the next step clear

Role and current brief

Link the approved posting, sourcing scope and recruiter responsible for changes. Use the current version when preparing updates or invitations.

Applicant and outreach status

Keep source, last contact, next action and any duplicate flag with the applicant record. Continue approved follow-ups and avoid a second message to the same person.

Interview and references

Record confirmed times, requested material and the owner for outstanding responses. Reschedule or follow up under the agreed rules and route exceptions.

Onboarding status

List approved next steps, deadlines and the HR, IT or training owner. Prepare the first-week handoff after the hiring decision is recorded.

Plan recruiting and people operations support around hiring stages

When a role opens

Confirm the posting version, LinkedIn candidate sourcing scope, calendar owner and response templates. Test an applicant record and an approved outreach draft before expanding the queue. Agree how to stop or revise the search if requirements change.

During interviews

Give the recruitment virtual assistant a predictable time to check replies and update scheduling. Keep an exception list for missed interviews, material still needed and unavailable panel members. Agree the alternate contact for changes close to the interview time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you source candidates through LinkedIn?

Yes, within the approved role criteria, permitted tools and access. We can research candidates and prepare outreach for your recruiter’s review.

Can a recruitment virtual assistant update our applicant tracking system?

We can maintain records, interview schedules and agreed status updates using the access you authorise.

Who decides which candidates move forward?

Your hiring team reviews candidate information and makes progression, selection and offer decisions.

Can you coordinate references or credentials?

We can request and track the agreed items through approved channels. Your reviewer decides how to assess them.

Can you help onboard a new employee?

We can coordinate the checklist for paperwork, calendars, training and access requests and flag anything waiting for an owner.

What can a weekly recruiting report include?

Open roles, applicant status, interviews due, outstanding references, onboarding tasks and the decisions your hiring team needs to make.
